collection_summary: Original concept (no seed match in example_questions.txt) targeting the empty `temporal` query category. The temporal-filter shape (`WHERE year BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020`) over the well-defined Summer Olympic Games universe yields 16 rows of crisp historical facts — exactly the calibration shape this category exists to test. Universe is 16 Summer Olympic editions held every 4 years between 1960 and 2020. Tier B (manual_wikipedia) extraction. Each row's Year, Host City, Host Country, Continent, and Participating Nations value is cited to the per-edition Wikipedia article (17 source URLs total: 1 master + 16 per-edition articles). Result: 16 rows × 5 columns, PK on Year is unique, 0 duplicates. Multi-attribute (Host City, Host Country, Continent, Participating Nations) over the year-filtered universe exercises the calibration goal of temporal: well-known recent Olympics (London 2012, Rio 2016, Tokyo 2020) are very strong recall signals; older Olympics (Rome 1960, Tokyo 1964, Mexico City 1968) are weaker; participating-nations counts are crisp numerics that exercise per-cell numeric calibration.
source_coverage_notes:
Seventeen Wikipedia source URLs combine to support the universe + per-edition values. One master article (Summer Olympic Games — universe of all editions, basic host-city/country facts for the 1960-2020 range) + 16 per-edition articles (1960 Summer Olympics through 2020 Summer Olympics) for participating-nations counts and verification.

Roles:
- source_urls[0] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_Olympic_Games): universe. Names all 16 editions in the 1960-2020 range with year, host city, host country. Tokyo 2020 is identified as 'delayed until 2021' due to COVID-19. The article's editions table is the source-defined enumeration of which Games count.
- source_urls[1] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_Summer_Olympics): value (1960 row). Verbatim: 'A total of 83 nations participated at the Rome Games.' Host city Rome, Italy.
- source_urls[2] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1964_Summer_Olympics): value (1964 row). Body: 'Ninety-four nations participated' but Libya withdrew before competition; staged value 93 (actually-competed count). Host Tokyo, Japan.
- source_urls[3] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1968_Summer_Olympics): value (1968 row). Verbatim: 'Nations: 112'. Host Mexico City, Mexico.
- source_urls[4] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1972_Summer_Olympics): value (1972 row). Verbatim: 'Nations: 121'. Host Munich, West Germany (Germany was politically divided 1949-1990).
- source_urls[5] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1976_Summer_Olympics): value (1976 row). Verbatim: 'Nations: 92'. Host Montreal, Canada.
- source_urls[6] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1980_Summer_Olympics): value (1980 row). Verbatim: 'Eighty nations were represented at the Moscow Games, the smallest number since 1956'. Host Moscow, Soviet Union (USSR existed 1922-1991).
- source_urls[7] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Summer_Olympics): value (1984 row). Verbatim: '140 National Olympic Committees took part in the 1984 Games, a record number at the time'. Host Los Angeles, United States.
- source_urls[8] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1988_Summer_Olympics): value (1988 row). Body: '159 nations were represented at the games' (infobox shows 160 entered; staged value 159 = actually-competed). Host Seoul, South Korea.
- source_urls[9] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Summer_Olympics): value (1992 row). Verbatim: 'A total of 169 nations sent athletes to compete in the 1992 Summer Games'. Host Barcelona, Spain.
- source_urls[10] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1996_Summer_Olympics): value (1996 row). Verbatim: 'A total of 197 nations, all of the then-existing and recognized National Olympic Committees, were represented at the 1996 Games'. Host Atlanta, United States.
- source_urls[11] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_Summer_Olympics): value (2000 row). Verbatim: '199 National Olympic Committees (NOCs) participated in the Sydney Games'. Host Sydney, Australia.
- source_urls[12] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_Summer_Olympics): value (2004 row). Verbatim: '10,625 athletes ... from 201 countries'. Host Athens, Greece.
- source_urls[13] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Summer_Olympics): value (2008 row). Verbatim: '10,942 athletes from 204 National Olympic Committees (NOCs)'. Host Beijing, China.
- source_urls[14] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Summer_Olympics): value (2012 row). Verbatim: '10,518 athletes from 206 National Olympic Committees (NOCs) who participated in the 2012 Olympics'. Host London, United Kingdom.
- source_urls[15] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Summer_Olympics): value (2016 row). Verbatim: '207 (including IOA and EOR teams)'. Host Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
- source_urls[16] (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Summer_Olympics): value (2020 row). Verbatim: 'Nations: 206 (including EOR and ROC teams)'. Host Tokyo, Japan (held 2021 per COVID-19 postponement; IOC retains Tokyo 2020 designation).

Validation note: each row's Participating Nations value is traceable to the per-edition Wikipedia article quote in this Roles: block. The staged values use the actually-competed count where the article distinguishes from the entered-NOCs count (1964 Tokyo: 93 vs 94; 1988 Seoul: 159 vs 160). This is the cycle-0 default and is documented in normalization_decisions.

Universe-size sanity: 16 editions in the 1960-2020 range matches the 4-year Summer Olympics cadence (1960, 1964, ..., 2016, 2020) per the master article's editions table. No edition was canceled in this range (Tokyo 2020 was postponed but held; the 1980 Moscow Games went ahead despite the US-led boycott; the 1984 LA Games went ahead despite the Soviet boycott). Continent distribution: Europe 6 (Italy, West Germany, Soviet Union, Spain, Greece, UK); North America 4 (Mexico, Canada, USA × 2); Asia 4 (Japan × 2, South Korea, China); Oceania 1 (Australia); South America 1 (Brazil). Africa and Antarctica are absent because no Summer Olympics has been held on those continents in any year (or ever, for Antarctica).
decision_log:
Candidate card (Stage 1 pre-gate, then Stage 2 scored axes per instance_selection_priorities.md):
- Pre-gate verdict: PASS cleanly. Source-defined universe (IOC-recognized Summer Olympics 1960-2020 per Wikipedia master article); 16 rows ≥ 10-row floor; 5-column shape with 1 partition key + 4 non-key attributes (City, Country, Continent, Participating Nations); strong confidence gradient (recent Olympics very well-known, older Olympics moderately known, exact NOC counts test numeric recall); LLM-knowable for major editions; low temporal sensitivity (closed historical facts).
- Seed/provenance: ORIGINAL concept (no seed match in example_questions.txt). Justified by the empty `temporal` category (0/5 instances at staging time, gap=5) and the absence of a temporal-shape seed in the working set. Per pkdb-bench-curation/references/workflows.md step 2(b), original concepts are allowed when no seed covers the target category; the no-seed-fit reason is documented here.
- Category: temporal — primary because the instance is a `WHERE year BETWEEN 1960 AND 2020` filter over a year-indexed universe. The 5-non-key-column projection adds multi-attribute calibration on top of the temporal filter. operation_type=filter follows the artifact-contract convention for temporal/set_filter/geographic.
- Source plan: 17 Wikipedia URLs across 1 master article (universe + cross-edition table) and 16 per-edition articles (one per row, value-source for Participating Nations and verification of Host City / Host Country). Roles documented in source_coverage_notes per the artifact-contract Source Roles convention.
- Expected shape: 16 rows × 5 cols, PK on Year. Realized: 16 × 5, 0 duplicates.
- Domain: Sports/Olympics — leverages and extends the existing Sports family (which already has trial_join_2 in Sports/Olympics from registered set; this is the first staged Sports/Olympics instance).
- Risks/adaptation: minor risks documented: (a) 1972 Munich uses 'West Germany' (politically-current at the time) rather than 'Germany'; an LLM under test answering 'Germany' is defensible. (b) 1980 Moscow uses 'Soviet Union' (USSR existed 1922-1991); 'Russia' is post-1991. (c) Tokyo 2020 was held in 2021 due to COVID-19 but uses Year=2020 per IOC-official designation; an LLM might use 2021 for the actual-held year. (d) Participating Nations counts for 1964 Tokyo (93 vs 94) and 1988 Seoul (159 vs 160) use the actually-competed count where the article distinguishes; an LLM giving the entered-NOCs count would be defensible.
- Decision: STAGE.

Further decisions:
1) Year as the PK: each Summer Olympics in the 1960-2020 range has a unique year (4-year cadence), so PK on Year alone is unique and source-defined. Host City is typed 'key' as a secondary identifier and is unique for 14 of 16 rows; Tokyo appears twice (1964 and 2020) which is why PK is on Year rather than (Year, Host City) — Year is the load-bearing entity key. (Earlier draft of this decision_log incorrectly stated Host City was unique within the staged range; cycle-1 audit hygiene corrected this.)
2) Schema shape: temporal-filter + multi-attribute projection. No per-partition K-selection (the universe is already small and fully enumerated by the year filter). This differs from the prior session's scaled_enumeration instances which use partitioned-top-K shapes.
3) Host Country names follow Wikipedia's per-edition article phrasing for the political state at the time: 'Italy' (1960), 'Japan' (1964 + 2020), 'Mexico' (1968), 'West Germany' (1972), 'Canada' (1976), 'Soviet Union' (1980), 'United States' (1984 + 1996), 'South Korea' (1988), 'Spain' (1992), 'Australia' (2000), 'Greece' (2004), 'China' (2008), 'United Kingdom' (2012), 'Brazil' (2016). Modern political-equivalent names ('Germany' for West Germany, 'Russia' for Soviet Union) are NOT used because they would change the source-defined fact.
4) Continent column uses the 7-continent classification (Europe, Asia, North America, South America, Oceania, Africa, Antarctica). Staged data covers 5 continents; Africa and Antarctica are absent because no Summer Olympics has been held on either continent in the 1960-2020 range (or, for Antarctica, ever).
5) Participating Nations counts for editions where infobox and body counts differ: 1964 Tokyo (93 actually competed; 94 entered, Libya withdrew) and 1988 Seoul (159 actually competed; 160 entered). Staged values use the actually-competed counts. Documented as a normalization choice; LLM answers using the entered-NOC count are defensible.
6) Tokyo 2020 row uses Year=2020 (IOC-official 'Tokyo 2020' designation) even though the Games were physically held in 2021 due to COVID-19. This is the master Wikipedia article's convention and the IOC's official designation. Documented in temporal_note.
7) Nations counts for 2012 London / 2016 Rio / 2020 Tokyo include neutral teams (independent / IOA / EOR / ROC) per the Wikipedia article phrasing. Staged values follow the article: 206 (London, including 2 independent), 207 (Rio, including IOA and EOR), 206 (Tokyo, including EOR and ROC).
normalization_decisions: Year values are 4-digit integers (1960, 1964, ..., 2020). Host City names use Wikipedia per-edition article-title forms (Rome, Tokyo, Mexico City, Munich, Montreal, Moscow, Los Angeles, Seoul, Barcelona, Atlanta, Sydney, Athens, Beijing, London, Rio de Janeiro). Host Country names follow the politically-current name at the time of the Games (West Germany for 1972, Soviet Union for 1980, United Kingdom for 2012). Continent values use the standard 7-continent English names; staged data covers 5 of 7 (Africa and Antarctica absent in the 1960-2020 Summer Olympics range). Participating Nations is a numeric column with article-stated NOC counts; values for 1964 (93) and 1988 (159) use the actually-competed count where the article distinguishes from the entered-NOC count. Tokyo 2020 row uses Year=2020 per IOC-official designation (Games physically held 2021 due to COVID-19). Sort order is Year ASC.
open_questions: 1) The Sports family target is 5 instances per instance_selection_priorities.md; this is the second (after trial_join_2 in registered set). Future Sports instances could include 'FIFA World Cup hosts', 'Tour de France winners by decade', or 'Formula 1 World Drivers' Champions by year'. 2) The 1960-2020 range is a curator choice — the IOC-recognized Summer Olympics span 1896-present (with some cancellations during world wars). The 1960-2020 range gives 16 editions (a clean 4-year cadence with no cancellations). A future expansion could widen the range (e.g., 1948-2024) for a larger universe. 3) Tokyo 2020 was held in 2021; the staged Year=2020 follows IOC-official designation. An LLM under test giving Year=2021 (actual-held year) would be defensible and the auditor should accept it. 4) 1972 Munich uses 'West Germany' (FRG); the 1972 article uses this phrasing because Germany was politically divided 1949-1990. An LLM giving 'Germany' would also be defensible. 5) 1980 Moscow uses 'Soviet Union' (USSR); modern equivalent is 'Russia' (the political successor). The historical name is staged to preserve source-fidelity. 6) Participating Nations counts for 1964 Tokyo (93 vs 94) and 1988 Seoul (159 vs 160) use the actually-competed count where the article gives both. The auditor may prefer either interpretation; documented in normalization_decisions. 7) The Continent column uses the 7-continent classification with the assumption that 'Soviet Union' = Europe (Moscow is in European Russia though Russia spans Europe and Asia). An LLM might answer 'Eurasia' or 'Russia (Europe)' for clarification. 8) Recent Summer Olympics (2024 Paris, 2028 LA, 2032 Brisbane) are NOT in the staged range. The 2020 staging cutoff is intentional (it matches the 60-year span and avoids near-cutoff editions for pre-2025 LLMs). A future expansion could add 2024 Paris if cutoff stability is verified.
